comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Architecture and plan for the evaldash issues, peer-reviewed as requested: https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6bfst8b/artifacts/evaldash-stats-engine (rev 2)

The four subissues are the same gap seen from four angles. Evaldash has no representation of *a measurement and how much of it happened* — a matrix cell is `value: float | None`, so there is nowhere to put "236 of 240 intended trials, 4 agent timeouts", and nothing to filter or aggregate on except presence. #8084 needs that representation to admit a partial run, #8085 needs it to qualify an aggregate, #8086 needs it to decide which result is admissible, #8087 needs a query object over it.

So the pre-work is one engine, shared by the eval runners and the dashboard: a typed measurement carrying its item counts and interval, plus an explicit selection query over a set of measurements. Each issue is then a call into it.

**Statistical core.** One estimand: the success rate over the items a run set out to grade. With `c = n_scored / n_attempted`, θ splits into an identified part and an unidentified one, and the missing part gets bounded rather than imputed — missingness correlates with task difficulty, which is exactly why #8084 needs a gate rather than an average. The reported interval is Wilson on the scored items, scaled by `c` and widened by `1 − c`, with an Imbens–Manski critical value so it covers the parameter at 95% instead of over-covering at ~97.5%. Width is at least `1 − c`: a run that graded 92.3% of its trials reports an interval at least 7.7 points wide however many trials it ran.

**Three things fall out that are worth flagging before implementation.**

1. Harbor already publishes a biased number, and the gate would expose it. `_aggregate` divides by `len(trials)` while an errored trial is read back with reward 0.0, so `accuracy` scores every timeout as a wrong answer — the Manski lower bound, computed by accident and labelled a point estimate. It is masked today only because any failed trial aborts the run. Relaxing that without fixing the denominator would ship the bias. The intended-trial count also cannot come from the result glob: a trial that dies before writing leaves no file, so the runs with the worst attrition would report perfect coverage.
2. Ranking cannot use `k / n_scored`. It is a complete-case estimate, so ranking on it rewards a model for timing out on hard items — #8085's complaint re-entering through the sort key. Ranking uses the interval's lower bound. At `c = 1` the two coincide, so the 368 evalchemy runs are unaffected.
3. A 90% gate admits results for display but cannot support ordering claims. Resolving a 5-point gap between two models needs coverage above 0.975 on both, and 2 points needs 0.99. Display admission and comparison admission are two thresholds, not one.

**Evidence.** Everything above is checked against the 387 records under `gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals` (CoreWeave needs credentials this session did not have). Item counts are already there — 1204 of 1249 per-task metric dicts carry `sample_len`, and Harbor carries `total`/`solved` — so the primary adapter is the record, not the archive, which matters because only 6 of 387 runs have a finestore archive today. A cross-check worth knowing about: the llama-3.1-8b mmlu record has 124 task entries because the run wrote the whole 62-entry panel twice, once under `mmlu_5shot` and once under a task directory named `tmp6jnnx8cc`, scoring 0.63502 and 0.63488. Benchmark identity cannot be the raw evalchemy task directory, and that duplicate looks like a separate launcher bug.

**Peer review** changed the design materially, so the artifact records it. Adopted: the Imbens–Manski correction; asymmetric difference bounds; demoting paired comparison, which provably buys zero attrition-width reduction; the Harbor denominator fixes; dropping a fleet-max denominator inference and a new Postgres table that would have been write-only; and moving the engine out of `lib/finestore` — `marin-core` already depends on `marin-finestore`, so an engine there naming `RunStatus` would create a distribution cycle and break that wheel's CI leg. It lives in `marin/evaluation/` under the same import-light contract as `records.py` and is vendored into the dashboard image by one `COPY`; "on top of finestore" holds on the data path, not the package path. One of my own claims did not survive: the apparent mmlu panel drift between models was my triple-count of group and leaf rows.

Proceeding to implementation as one PR: engine and tests, the record coverage contract, the Harbor gate, the evaldash panel API, then the SPA. Item-level tallies, paired comparison intervals, and evidence-based suspect-zero detection are deferred and will be filed separately.

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Plan and first PR are up.

**Artifact (architecture + plan, peer-reviewed twice):** https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6bfst8b/artifacts/evaldash-stats-engine
**PR:** #8122 — CI green.

## What the four issues have in common

evaldash had no representation of *a measurement and how much of it happened* — a cell was `value: float | None`. That single gap produces all four symptoms: a Harbor batch with one timed-out trial in 240 is either discarded or silently scored as if the trial were wrong (#8084); a cross-benchmark mean is reported without saying which benchmarks, at which metric, or what it did about the ones a model never ran (#8085); a partial re-run hides older results that are still the newest available for their own benchmark (#8086); and filtering has nowhere to express "complete coverage only" because coverage isn't a thing the data carries (#8087).

So the PR is mostly the engine, with the four issues as applications of it — the pre-work-plus-applications shape you suggested, in one PR rather than five.

## The engine

Each result is stored as sufficient statistics (items graded, items attempted, correct count, recorded dispersion, per-cause counts of ungraded items) and intervals are derived on read. The estimand is θ over the items a run *set out* to grade. With `c = n_scored / n_attempted`, `θ = c·θ_obs + (1−c)·θ_miss`, and θ_miss is bounded to [0, 1] rather than imputed — a trial that times out is more likely to be a hard trial, so imputing anything for it is a guess about difficulty. The interval therefore widens by at least `1−c`: admitting a partial batch costs width proportional to what was missed, which is your "unknown interval around the missed answers" made concrete.

Two details worth flagging:

- The critical value is Imbens–Manski, not the ordinary 1.96. Applying the two-sided quantile to an interval that already spans an unidentified region covers the identified *set* at 95% and over-covers the parameter (~97.5% at realistic coverage rates). Because Δ is known exactly here rather than estimated, the usual objection to that correction doesn't apply.
- Binary metrics use Wilson, because eval results really do sit at the boundary — 0 of 8 agentic trials has a normal interval of *zero width* and a Wilson interval of [0.000, 0.324].

Every ordering in the system sorts on the interval's lower bound, so losing items cannot buy rank.

## Per issue

**#8084** — Harbor takes its attempted-trial count from the job's own bookkeeping (counting result files misses every trial that died before writing one, so preempted runs would report perfect coverage), divides rates by the trials a verifier actually graded, and keeps the per-error-type counts of the rest. A batch below a 90% completion gate fails as `infra_failed` and still records its coverage, so the rejection reads as counts. Run detail shows the breakdown. An unreadable job record leaves the count *unknown* rather than equal to results-found — the runs where it's unknown are exactly the interrupted ones a found-count would certify as complete.

**#8085** — No cross-benchmark mean is shown at all unless a caller names a missing-data policy, and one that is shown renders its panel, per-benchmark metrics, and policy inline. The primary surface is a panel table: one row per model, one column per benchmark. `ComparePage`'s client-side mean, which scored a missing shared benchmark as 0, is gone; comparison goes through the engine and answers orderings with a difference interval per benchmark rather than two error bars to eyeball.

**#8086** — Each benchmark comes from the newest run that clears the request's admission rules, across cohorts, so a partial re-run no longer hides results still newest for their own benchmark. `cohort=` pins to one launch when you want that instead. Every cell carries its run id, version, git sha, and timestamp; a `(model, benchmark)` with no admitted cell reports why and links the offending run, so an empty cell is explained rather than blank.

**#8087** — Benchmark column selection, a one-action complete-panel filter, cohort selection, model search, and run-metadata facets (accelerator/platform/backend/mechanism/user) are all in the request, so a panel is a shareable URL. The active ones render as removable chips: a number on screen should never be the product of a filter the reader can't see.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Filed as follow-ups: item-level tallies so binary intervals stop depending on inverting a rate (#8123), paired comparisons on shared items (#8124), the evalchemy launcher writing the same mmlu panel under two task directories (#8125), attempted-item counts for lm-eval runs so their intervals stop being sampling-only (#8126), and pyrefly/test-selection coverage for the evaldash server tree (#8127).

One caveat on #8126 worth knowing before reading the dashboard: today nearly every evalchemy run's interval is labelled `sampling_only`, because lm-eval records how many documents it graded but never how many it attempted. That's the honest label — completeness is unknown, not established — but it applies fleet-wide until the producers record the count.

comments.body:
🤖 #8122 is merged (`fb91b3dc94`). #8084, #8085, #8086 and #8087 closed with it; leaving this thread open for whatever comes next.

What landed, briefly. Every eval score now carries an interval that covers the items its run did not grade, from one engine (`marin.evaluation.eval_stats`) that the producers and evaldash share. The estimand is fixed once — θ over the items a run set out to grade — and the unobserved part is bounded rather than imputed, so admitting a partial run costs interval width instead of quietly biasing the number upward. Every ordering sorts on the lower bound.

Two things worth knowing if you use the panel:

**evalchemy results are no longer "completeness unknown."** lm-eval publishes no attempted-item count beside its metrics, so the honest reading of every evalchemy run was sampling error with unknown completeness. Its per-sample rows do carry the document indices it enumerated, so the export pass that was already reading those files now derives the attempted count, the pass tally, and the count of items whose grader extracted no answer. That moves the fleet onto identified intervals.

**A benchmark where nothing parseable came back is held out of the panel** rather than standing as a model's newest score. The zero is real, but it is equally consistent with a broken grader, and publishing a collapse on that basis is the same error as hiding it. The cell reads `flagged` and links the run; `include_flagged=1` admits it.

Also folded in: Harbor's 90% infrastructure gate with its per-cause error counts, cross-cohort merge of the newest valid result per benchmark, benchmark-column selection with a one-action complete-panel filter, and `/api/compare` answering orderings with a difference interval instead of two error bars.

Not done, and the honest gap: comparisons are not paired on the items both runs actually graded. That needs a join across two sample archives per request. Worth filing when someone wants it.

Design and rationale: https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6bfst8b/artifacts/evaldash-stats-engine

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Allow Grug MoE backends to exclude padded positions from expert dispatch, capacity accounting, and expert computation. Carry token validity from the model's attention mask into the MoE path; a padding token ID alone is not sufficient because the same ID can appear at a valid position.

In the Snowball 67B RL trial on 32 H100s (PP4/EP8, ragged all-to-all, capacity factor 2), the first microbatch contained 42,435 padded positions out of 68,160 (62.26%). Routing rejected 1,559,713 of 7,088,640 assignments across 26 layers, and the no-drop guard stopped the run before an optimizer update. Padding contributes to capacity demand; the fraction of rejected assignments belonging to valid tokens has not been measured. The ragged backend reports these as sender drops, although clipping is applied to receiver expert-chunk capacity.

Packing is being added separately. For the complete 512-trajectory capture, Levanter's packing reduces overall padding from 55.10% to 15.49% after alignment to eight GPUs, so residual padding still needs handling.

Done when:

- Invalid positions consume no expert capacity and produce no dispatched expert rows or expert-parameter gradient contributions.
- When valid assignments fit capacity, valid-token outputs, loss, and gradients match an equivalent unpadded, dropless computation within existing numerical tolerances. Adding padding does not change which valid assignments are accepted, including when valid demand exceeds capacity.
- Tests cover mixed sequence lengths, packed segment boundaries, all-padding local shards, and distributed forward/backward execution without collective mismatches.
- Routing metrics distinguish valid assignments, skipped padding, and genuine capacity drops. A padded workload benchmark reports the memory and runtime effect.

Start with `moe_mlp` in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py` and the ragged backend in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`.

Evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/users/dlwh/skyrl/migration/june-ragged-67b-benchmark-20260907-02/drops.json`, `capture-padding.json` under the same prefix, and `s3://marin-us-east-02a/users/dlwh/skyrl/migration/june-packing-census-20260907-01/census.json`.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read fix-issue and commit skills, AGENTS.md
- [x] Investigate Grug MoE dispatch/capacity path and how token validity flows
- [x] Assess scope — feature-scale (multi-backend + metrics + distributed tests + benchmark), no PR
- [x] Post root-cause analysis and proposed approach

## Research

The MoE path has no concept of token validity. `moe_mlp` and every EP backend accept only `x [T,D]`, `selected_experts [T,K]`, and `combine_weights [T,K]`; padded positions are ordinary rows and route like any token ([`grug_moe.py` L146-161](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L146-L161)). In the ragged backend, demand is `group_sizes = bincount(flat_selected, length=num_experts)` and capacity is `ceil(capacity_factor * tokens_per_shard * topk)`, so padded assignments count as real demand, get clipped against capacity, are dispatched and run through the expert MLP, and contribute expert-parameter gradients ([`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py` L328-345](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L328-L345)). The reported drops are then `sum(group_sizes) - accepted_local`, which conflates padding with genuine capacity drops of valid tokens ([L420-422](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L420-L422)) — consistent with the 62% padding and 22% rejected-assignments observation and the no-drop guard tripping. As the issue notes, a padding token id cannot identify padding (the same id can appear at a valid position), so validity must come from the attention mask / segment ids.

## Proposed approach (for review before implementation)

Thread an optional validity mask and make invalid positions consume no capacity, no dispatched rows, and no expert-parameter gradients, while keeping all buffer shapes statically sized on the worst case so no collective shapes change.

1. **API.** Add `token_valid: Bool[Array, "T"] | None = None` to `MoEExpertMlp.__call__` → `moe_mlp` → each `_moe_mlp_ep_*_local` and `_moe_mlp_local`. `None` means all-valid, preserving current behavior and existing tests. Derive the mask in the model from the attention mask / segment ids (grug attention already exposes `segment_ids` metadata via `thd_segment_metadata_from_segment_ids`).
2. **Ragged backend.** Before `bincount`, remap invalid tokens' `flat_selected` to a sentinel expert (`num_experts`) so `bincount(length=num_experts)` drops them from `group_sizes`. Their sorted assignments land past every real group, so `_expert_granular_a2a_params` never sends them — no receiver capacity, no dispatched rows, no expert-param grads. `[TK]`/`[C]` buffers stay static; only the counts feeding `group_sizes`/clipping change. Zero invalid tokens' `combine_weights` as belt-and-suspenders (the unpermute already reads unwritten slots as zero).
3. **Other backends.** Apply the equivalent capacity-accounting exclusion to `ep_fixed_all_to_all`, `ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, `ep_ring`, `ep_deepep`, and `local` — each computes capacity/clipping differently.
4. **Metrics.** Extend `CapacityOverflow` (or the routing metrics) to distinguish valid assignments dispatched, skipped-padding assignments, and genuine capacity drops of valid tokens, replacing the padding-conflated `dropped_local`.
5. **Invariants to preserve** (from Done-when): with `token_valid=None` outputs are bit-identical to today; when valid demand fits capacity, valid outputs/loss/grads match an unpadded dropless reference within existing tolerances; adding padding never changes which valid assignments are accepted (the sentinel keeps valid group prefixes and clip decisions independent of padding).
6. **Tests / benchmark.** Mixed sequence lengths, packed segment boundaries, an all-padding local shard (zero output, no collective mismatch), and distributed forward/backward equivalence vs. an unpadded reference; plus a padded-workload benchmark reporting memory and runtime.

Files: `grug_moe.py`, `_moe/{ep_ragged_all_to_all,ep_fixed_all_to_all,ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all,ep_ring,ep_deepep,local,common}.py`, and the training MoE MLP block that threads the mask. Scope spans multiple backends and distributed tests, so this is larger than a self-contained fix; handing it to a human to confirm the sentinel-remap design and metric shape before implementation.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Research

No open PR overlaps #8953. Each Grug block passes the attention mask to attention, then calls the MoE with activations alone ([hero EP block](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1106-L1128), [MoE API](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L117-L161)). The ragged backend counts every flattened assignment before capacity clipping ([ragged dispatch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L328-L345)), while capacity metrics expose only sender and receiver drops ([capacity type](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/common.py#L130-L139)).

Proposed Fix

Derive token validity from the attention mask's query segment IDs and thread it through routing and every MoE backend. Keep collective and buffer shapes static, but exclude invalid assignments from expert group counts, capacity ranks, combine weights, and expert gradients; report skipped assignments separately from genuine capacity drops. Add value/gradient regressions for mixed lengths, packed boundaries, all-padding shards, and distributed execution, plus a padded-workload benchmark that reports runtime and memory.

The pull request separates skipped padding from sender and receiver drops, adds distributed and compact-equivalence coverage, and includes a fresh-process runtime and memory benchmark.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
## Summary

The region-replicated **`nemotron_mix` tokenized cache** is **not byte-identical across regions**, even though the cache paths are content-addressed (`tokenized/<component>-<hash>/...`, which should guarantee identical replicas). In `gs://marin-eu-west4`, two of the nine components — **`starcoderdata-12f018`** and **`proofpile_2-4a35c7`** — diverge from the `gs://marin-us-east5` reference in both their `shard_ledger.json` content **and** their underlying shard-object counts. `proofpile_2` in `eu-west4` looks **~90% incomplete** (373 train objects vs 3497 in us-east5).

A real grug-MoE training run on a `europe-west4` v6e slice reading `gs://marin-eu-west4` **crashed during cache load**:

```
levanter.store.cache  Attempting to load cache ledger from gs://marin-eu-west4/tokenized/nemotron_cc/...
...
Exception: EOF while parsing a string at line 252508 column 9
  File ".../levanter/data/text/datasets.py", line 975, in build_caches
    cache = load_lm_dataset_cache(cache_path, component.format, self.the_tokenizer, ...)
RuntimeError: Step failed: grug/sparsity/...-k16-...
```

## Evidence (reproducible with `gsutil`)

**Ledger content — 7/9 identical across regions, 2 diverge** (`gsutil cat .../train/shard_ledger.json | md5sum`):

| component | eu-west4 md5 / bytes | us-east5 md5 / bytes | |
|---|---|---|---|
| nemotron_cc/hq_actual-5af4cc | 0c70f90a / 182158 | 0c70f90a / 182158 | ✅ identical |
| nemotron_cc/hq_synth-3525e2 | 95c2bd7a / 964455 | 95c2bd7a / 964455 | ✅ |
| nemotron_cc/medium_high-d21701 | afce5109 / 162292 | afce5109 / 162292 | ✅ |
| nemotron_cc/medium-d86506 | b0b65011 / 639077 | b0b65011 / 639077 | ✅ |
| nemotron_cc/medium_low-0fdb07 | a271735e / 283271 | a271735e / 283271 | ✅ |
| nemotron_cc/low_actual-cb3f2c | a364578e / 129952 | a364578e / 129952 | ✅ |
| nemotron_cc/low_synth-3c57b3 | 4312d8c4 / 118336 | 4312d8c4 / 118336 | ✅ |
| **starcoderdata-12f018** | **4af4dba5 / 174739** | **7b017f24 / 78987** | ❌ **differs** |
| **proofpile_2-4a35c7** | **a082d5d2 / 22582** | **5be85fed / 42103** | ❌ **differs** |

**Underlying shard data also diverges** (`gsutil ls '.../train/**' | wc -l`):

| component | eu-west4 train objects | us-east5 train objects |
|---|---|---|
| starcoderdata-12f018 | 14054 | 7962 |
| proofpile_2-4a35c7 | **373** | **3497** |

So this is not just a metadata/ledger mismatch — the eu-west4 replicas of these two components contain a **different (and for `proofpile_2`, largely missing) set of shards**.

Repro:
```bash
for c in starcoderdata-12f018 proofpile_2-4a35c7; do
  echo "== $c =="
  gsutil cat gs://marin-eu-west4/tokenized/$c/train/shard_ledger.json | md5sum
  gsutil cat gs://marin-us-east5/tokenized/$c/train/shard_ledger.json | md5sum
  echo "eu objs: $(gsutil ls 'gs://marin-eu-west4/tokenized/'$c'/train/**' | wc -l)"
  echo "e5 objs: $(gsutil ls 'gs://marin-us-east5/tokenized/'$c'/train/**' | wc -l)"
done
```

## Impact

- **Cross-region runs are not reproducible**: a run reading `eu-west4` trains on different `starcoderdata`/`proofpile_2` data than the same config in `us-east5`.
- **Runs reading `eu-west4` can hard-fail on cache load** (the `EOF while parsing` above; consistent with a partially-replicated component).
- Practically, `us-east5` is currently the only region with a `nemotron_mix` cache that loads cleanly. This bites on v6e specifically, since v6e exists only in `europe-west4-a` / `us-east1-d` / `us-east5-b`, and the `us-east1` cache is *also* partial (2/9 ledgers present) — so a v6e job that gets squeezed out of `us-east5` capacity has no good fallback region.

## Notes / possible cause

- All nine ledgers individually parse as valid JSON via `gsutil cat` today, so the `EOF while parsing` the job hit may have been a truncated streaming read of the incomplete `proofpile_2`/`starcoder` data, rather than a corrupt-but-complete ledger.
- The 7 `nemotron_cc` components replicated correctly (md5-identical), so whatever populated `eu-west4` either ran before `starcoder`/`proofpile_2` finished, or copied a different build of just those two.

## Ask

1. Re-replicate (or re-validate) the `eu-west4` `nemotron_mix` caches against the `us-east5` source — at minimum `starcoderdata-12f018` and `proofpile_2-4a35c7`.
2. Consider a content-integrity check (size/md5 manifest, or shard-count vs ledger) as part of cross-region cache replication, so divergent/partial replicas are detected rather than surfacing as a mid-training `EOF` crash.
3. Worth auditing `us-east1` and the other replicas (`us-central1`, `us-central2`, `us-west4`) the same way — I only verified `us-east5` (good) and `eu-west4` (bad) end-to-end.

Found while running strong-sparsity grug-MoE experiments. cc @ravwojdyla

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — not opening a PR (ops + design work, not a self-contained code bug).**

# Research

The eu-west4 bucket holds a *partial/divergent* copy of two content-addressed components (`starcoderdata-12f018`, `proofpile_2-4a35c7`). Content addressing keys the cache path on the **build config**, not the **output bytes**, so a second build (or a half-finished copy) with the same config lands at the same `tokenized/<component>-<hash>/` path and silently overwrites/partially-fills it. Nothing on the load path verifies that the shard objects physically present under the cache match what `shard_ledger.json` claims, so a partial replica either trains on the wrong data or dies mid-read (`EOF while parsing`).

The cache load path trusts the ledger + whatever objects exist; the only validation (`_validate_sharded_ledger`) checks the ledger's *internal* arithmetic (row/field-count sums), **not** that the referenced shard objects exist or are complete on storage. `build_caches` only catches `FileNotFoundError` (missing ledger) — a present-but-incomplete shard set is not detected.

**Relevant code**
- [`store/cache.py#L598-L611`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/store/cache.py#L598-L611) — `CacheLedger.load`: reads `shard_ledger.json`, no object-presence check
- [`store/cache.py#L618-L656`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/store/cache.py#L618-L656) — `_validate_sharded_ledger`: only ledger self-consistency, never lists shards on storage
- [`data/text/datasets.py#L956-L966`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L956-L966) — load-or-rebuild: only `FileNotFoundError` triggers rebuild; partial shards pass through
- [`data/text/cache.py#L44`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/cache.py#L44) — `load_lm_dataset_cache` entry point
- [`scripts/ops/cross_region.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/scripts/ops/cross_region.py) — cross-region tooling *analyzes* egress only; **no replication or integrity step exists** (replication is manual `gsutil`)
- [`experiments/pretraining_datasets/nemotron.py#L49-L56`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/pretraining_datasets/nemotron.py#L49-L56) — content-addressed override paths for the affected components

# Proposed approach (for a human to review before implementation)

Two parts; both need a human — the first is cross-region data movement I'm not permitted to do (AGENTS.md), the second is new tooling/design.

1. **Ops (immediate, needs region-egress sign-off):** re-copy `starcoderdata-12f018` and `proofpile_2-4a35c7` from `gs://marin-us-east5` → `gs://marin-eu-west4`, then re-validate md5/object-count parity per the issue's repro. Audit `us-east1`, `us-central1`, `us-central2`, `us-west4` the same way. Deleting the bad replicas to force `auto_build_caches` rebuild is the costly fallback (re-tokenization).

2. **Tooling (the reviewable deliverable):** add a `validate_cache(cache_path)` that, given a sharded cache, lists storage and checks every `finished_shard` in the ledger has its expected `part-NNNNN-of-MMMMM/` objects present (count/size), reporting any shard the ledger claims but storage is missing. Expose it as a `scripts/ops/` CLI usable as a **post-replication gate** and a **cross-region audit**. Open question for reviewers: also wire a lightweight presence check into the load path so a partial replica fails fast with a clear error instead of a mid-training EOF — at the cost of extra (cross-region) list ops per cache. Recommend the standalone gate first; load-path check opt-in.

cc @ravwojdyla — confirm the desired direction (standalone validator vs. load-path enforcement) and who owns the eu-west4 re-replication.

## TL;DR

Launch the cleaned Datakit SFT mixture from the 67B/2B-active long-context checkpoint at step 157,000. The run uses 80% SFT and 20% pretraining replay for 2,000 steps on a non-preemptible v4-2048.

## Description

The SFT sources are normalized to a common chat schema, repaired per source, rendered with the Marin chat template, and tokenized with `marin-community/marin-tokenizer`. Whole conversations use Levanter's existing greedy packing path: another conversation is added only when it fits in the remaining context. Attention and loss are blocked across conversation boundaries.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Produce the first production checkpoint trained on the cleaned Datakit chat mixture while retaining 20% long-context pretraining replay.

## Status

Ready to submit from commit `77308d1a9fc61afd226f5cf98a6dabc14f1be39f`. The output root is unused and the step-157000 source checkpoint is complete.

At the same 8k budget, Datakit scores 27.67%. The longer-budget result is not a controlled improvement over that baseline.

The table compares those two checkpoints, rather than selecting a different winning model for each benchmark. Scores are percentages from completed evaluation records.

| Benchmark / metric | Snowball Nemotron-Terminal SFT | Datakit SFT step 159,000 |
|---|---:|---:|
| AIME24, 8k | 37.00 (111/300) | 27.67 (83/300) |
| AIME24, 32k | — | 38.67 (116/300) |
| AIME24, 262k | — | 35.56 (64/180), **partial** |
| MATH500 | 78.20 | 69.40 |
| MMLU, 5-shot accuracy | 73.50 | 74.89 |
| GSM8K, 0-shot flexible extraction | 85.75 | 84.91 |
| ARC-Challenge, 25-shot normalized accuracy | 66.47 | 68.26 |

| TriviaQA, 5-shot extracted exact match | 39.90 | 22.57 |
| OlympiadBench, legacy 30-question subset | 11.00 | 12.33 |

AIME uses 30 questions with ten planned repetitions. The 262k recovery timed out after 44 hours with six responses per question saved. Of those 180 responses, 147 (81.7%) hit the token limit and 108 (60.0%) hit it without a boxed answer. Grading uses the pinned evaluator's unchanged answer extraction; no answer repair was applied. The actual requests used temperature 0, seed 1234, and an effective output cap of 261,056 tokens within the 262,144-token context.

Recovery job `/held/aime262k-stream-resume-20260914-r3` has replayed all 180 saved responses and started the remaining 120 on the existing CoreWeave H100 server. Request payloads must exactly match the original settings. The evaluator timeout is now 72 hours. Estimated remaining runtime is about 29 hours; the 35.56% score remains partial until all 300 are graded.

Datakit's completed agentic results on `DCAgent/dev_set_v2` are 16/289 (5.54%) for fixed-template OpenCode with compaction and 13/300 (4.33%) for Terminus 2 with thinking disabled. The later OpenCode sampling run and mini-SWE-agent run failed the grading-completeness gate, so neither provides a final score. These agent/harness settings differ; the percentages do not isolate model quality.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Establish a reproducible baseline for an existing Snowball terminal agent on established computational biology benchmarks, with frozen weights. Start with a small diagnostic pilot, then expand to a fixed evaluation set for comparing subsequent checkpoints. Use the results to identify useful biology training targets and separate scientific errors from agent, serving, environment, and grading failures.

## Description

Computational biology tasks combine coding, statistical analysis, scientific judgment, and domain tools. Snowball already has a post-trained terminal-agent checkpoint and measured performance with its matching harness in [#8225](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8225). We need to establish how that capability transfers to biological analysis.

The proposed starting model is [Snowball 67B-A2B Nemotron-Terminal, step 1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888/tree/680bec3ade494b61ead6861fa24fc4071f8dc294), evaluated through Harbor with its matching Terminus-2 terminal-agent harness. Confirm whether a newer checkpoint is preferred before fixing the baseline. Record each checkpoint separately.

Use Marin's existing evaluation launcher and Harbor integration where available. This issue tracks benchmark selection, integration readiness, runs, and findings. Substantial adapter changes can be linked as separate implementation work. New benchmarks, training, and tool-free biology evaluations are outside the first milestone.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure how often Snowball completes computational biology tasks under a fixed execution budget, and identify the dominant causes of failure. The initial baseline measures existing capability; it does not establish the causal benefit of coding training or imply an absence of biology exposure in the checkpoint's training data.

The first two candidates are the proposed readiness checks for a small pilot without a personal OpenAI API key. The remaining candidates need additional access, grading, integration, or runtime planning. Scorer code and release inventories were checked on 2026-09-14. A hosted scoring service, released grading code, and answer rubrics provide different integration options. Except for the GeneBench-Pro scorer checks below, these are source inspections; no end-to-end agent evaluation has run.

| Benchmark and capability | Released scorer and reference material | Access and judge requirements | Harbor readiness |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Terminal-Bench-Science, life sciences](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science): scientific workflows | Task-specific executable tests and reference fixtures are released. For the inspected [genomic-model-ranking task](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science/tree/ff55a1b0810a5cc2ebac3ebb007cbe6a26aa2e3b/tasks/life-sciences/biology/genomic-model-ranking/tests), pytest checks predictions, rankings, and executable submissions against supplied fixtures and thresholds. | That task's verifier runs without network access or a judge API. Check other tasks individually. | Harbor-native. First readiness check; validate compatibility with Marin's pinned Harbor and measure runtime before selecting more tasks. |
| [GeneBench-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package): judgment-heavy genomics and quantitative biology | Ten public cases include [reference_grader.py](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package/blob/eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2/reference_grader.py), reference answers, schemas, and tolerances. Uses numeric, integer, and exact-match checks. Boolean `passed` is authoritative; `score` is diagnostic. | Ungated public package; grader uses the Python standard library and no API key. The full 129-task suite is not contained in this release. | No adapter found. Concrete candidate for a small port: scorer checks passed below. Public cases support development and reproduction, with results reported separately from the full benchmark. |
| [CompBioBench](https://github.com/Genentech/compbiobench-runner): 100 tasks across omics, genetics, and ML | Official hosted scorer uses whitespace-stripped exact string match. Public runner and input dataset are released; no downloadable official scorer or answer key was found. The [leaderboard code](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Genentech/compbiobench-leaderboard-v1/blob/6a63e6d2cae531d9e9bf46b341606ed6b304ba3f/app.py) delegates grading to a separate evaluator that is not publicly accessible. | Hosted submission requires Hugging Face login, answers for all 100 questions, and currently allows two submissions per user per day. No OpenAI judge key is specified. | No adapter found. Full-suite hosted scoring is available through the documented submission path. A self-contained local verifier or small-subset scorer still needs author support. |
| [BixBench v1.5, Harbor CLI](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/adapters/bixbench): notebook-derived biological analysis questions | [Harbor judge code](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/0d67ca4b59206aca2734bf9fe0260ca79e08acb4/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) and public reference answers are available. The adapter grades open answers with an LLM, including numeric/range answers. Upstream also releases a [deterministic multiple-choice grader](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/49311180bdacb324c596f2e07596c126f2004008/bixbench/graders.py). | Current Harbor grader requires OpenAI access. Upstream multiple-choice scoring needs no judge API, but uses a different question/answer protocol. | Adapter exists upstream and in Marin's fork. Current CLI route is conditional on judge access. Multiple-choice grading is not the current Harbor CLI protocol. |
| [BioMysteryBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/BioMysteryBench-full): analysis of anonymized biological datasets | Reference answers and criteria are supplied in `answer_rubric`. No official executable scorer was found in the release inventory or Anthropic GitHub search. Community scorers exist, but their equivalence to Anthropic's scoring is unverified. | Full 90-task release is gated and evaluation-only; five preview tasks and their rubrics are accessible. Rubrics require both a correct answer and compliance with the source-lookup policy, so checking answer text alone is insufficient. | No adapter found. Requires a specified grading procedure, such as documented expert review for a small diagnostic pilot; automated score comparability remains unresolved. |
| [LABBench2](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2): broad research skills, including literature, sequences, and cloning | [HybridEvaluator](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2/blob/c028ecdcf144b55ffcd92b68be45081df5628c20/evals/evaluators.py) and sequence/cloning validators are released. Dataset includes answer and validator metadata; external reference files are resolved by the runner. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. `seqqa2` and `cloning` use executable grading. Other categories use an LLM judge, defaulting to Anthropic; even the implementation named `exact_match_evaluator` calls an LLM. | No LABBench2 adapter found. Existing Harbor `labbench` covers original LAB-Bench FigQA. Selected sequence tasks could supply a complementary evaluation after integration. |
| [BixBench3](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3): 20 research-scale analyses from raw data | [Artifact scorer](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3/blob/d0e0bbb41222335b1b8878f533a58466a3a782dc/src/bixbench3/grading/grader.py) is released, with reference artifact packages on GCS. `bixbench3 grade` scores existing artifacts deterministically. A separate process judge evaluates the analysis trajectory. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. Artifact scoring itself uses no LLM; the standard cloud runner requires OpenAI for process review and web-access decisions. Full artifact downloads were not tested. | Standalone runner; no adapter found. Later workflow evaluation, with data and runtime costs measured explicitly. |

Choose the first suite by scientific relevance, integration effort, grading availability, and measured cost. Record whether an LLM is needed for correctness grading, process review, or other runner functions. Check for in-progress ports before starting a new adapter.

Prioritize two concrete readiness checks without an OpenAI judge dependency: validate Terminal-Bench-Science's existing Harbor task, or port one to three GeneBench-Pro public cases using their released scorer. Integrate additional tasks before expanding to a measured pilot that excludes the development smoke tests. The inspected `genomic-model-ranking` task specifies 2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM, no GPU, and an eight-hour agent limit. These are declared requirements, not measured pilot costs. CompBioBench is a candidate for full-suite hosted evaluation; its public release does not currently supply the local scorer needed by the proposed small pilot. Reconsider BixBench if the project provides judge access; substituting a different judge requires validation and a separately identified evaluation variant.

Scorer validation: at GeneBench-Pro release `eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2`, the reference grader accepted the published reference answer for all 10 cases and rejected deliberately wrong and empty answer objects for all 10. These 30 checks ran locally without an API or analysis data. They validate the grading interface, not the scientific analyses. The documented command is `python3 reference_grader.py <eval_config.json> <eval_answer.json>`. A future adapter must expose only the task, answer schema, and analysis inputs to the agent; keep the full config, references, tolerances, reports, and grader outside its workspace.

## Status

Planning. No computational biology baseline has been run as part of this effort. Primary benchmark, evaluation owner, serving support, spending cap, and completion date are unconfirmed. The proposed October 6, 2026 release of post-trained 67B Snowball motivates obtaining a baseline early enough to guide biology follow-up work. The first run date depends on access and readiness.

First milestone:

- [ ] Select a primary benchmark and record the checkpoint, evaluation owner, serving contact, budget, and target date.
- [ ] Confirm a working endpoint or serving allocation, sandbox access, and any grader credentials. Budget serving time, sandbox task-hours, grading, setup, and retries separately.
- [ ] Pin model/tokenizer, Marin/Harbor, dataset, and container revisions. Record prompts, tools/network policy, sampling, context management, context/step/time limits, judge settings, and retry policy.
- [ ] Validate one or two development tasks: reference answers pass, deliberately wrong answers fail, missing submissions are accounted for, and a real analysis can execute. Keep reference answers, solutions, and verifier material inaccessible to the solving agent. The BixBench oracle writes an answer directly, so it checks grading without reproducing the analysis.
- [ ] Run one prespecified task once and measure serving time, sandbox time, and grading cost. Expand to 5–10 prespecified tasks only after checking the measured cost against the pilot budget; retain the first task in that pilot. Exclude the development smoke-test tasks from the measured pilot. For BixBench, select questions from distinct data capsules (separate source notebooks and their associated data) and record their IDs before examining their Snowball results.
- [ ] Publish configs, trajectories, produced artifacts, success counts, coverage, runtime/cost, and a short failure analysis. Report successes over all scheduled attempts and over attempts with a determined model outcome. Coverage is the fraction of scheduled attempts with a determined model outcome. Count agent-caused missing submissions and timeouts as failures unless a retained verifier result establishes success. Exclude unresolved infrastructure and grader errors only from the second denominator; report their counts and coverage separately.
- [ ] Decide whether to expand the primary suite, repair the harness, or validate a second benchmark. Record the evidence and follow-up owner.

For subsequent checkpoint comparisons, hold the task set, harness, and execution budget fixed. Keep inspected development tasks separate from an untouched final evaluation set. Preserve each baseline and record protocol changes. Evaluation-only materials and inspected evaluation trajectories must stay out of training.

Treat all ten public GeneBench-Pro cases as development and reproduction material for this effort. Any final set whose results have not guided model or protocol changes must be selected separately before follow-on training; the initial pilot does not supply that final set.

Count each fresh agent rollout, including retries, as a separate attempt and report first-attempt success separately. Regrading an existing submission does not create a new agent attempt.

## Links

- Planning context: [Bio-Snowball proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UnoAHNlkRAskxC9fAnF1SMpiU4QnFg-A8x9aXoEQ_MI/edit?tab=t.x53y2cvqravy).
- Starting assets: [Snowball SFT and evaluations, #8225](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8225), [archived serving and agent configurations](https://gist.github.com/penfever/34e22b004327aa220ccdcfc87b29a0ec/cfeaa1ad862586676f4de189cc2e8bcf067ea2f5).
- Evaluation integration: [launcher documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/README.md), [evaluation architecture discussion, #7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345).
- Benchmark discovery: [Harbor Hub](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets?scope=all), [upstream adapters](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/adapters), [Marin's Harbor fork](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/main/adapters).
- Run artifacts and reports: add as runs complete; keep raw logs and dense results in the artifact store.

## Decision Log

2026-09-14: Plan the pilot without requiring a personal OpenAI API key. Make BixBench conditional on project-provided judge access, which has not been arranged, and prioritize a readiness check of an existing Harbor-native task with executable grading. The primary suite and execution budget remain unconfirmed.

2026-09-14 scorer audit: distinguish CompBioBench's documented full-suite hosted scoring from its unavailable local scorer. Add GeneBench-Pro's public cases as a concrete porting option after 30 successful scorer checks. No agent runs, hosted submissions, or gated-data access requests were made in this audit.

## Conclusion

Pending baseline results.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
The TaskTrove clean release exposed an incomplete boundary between converted Harbor tasks and post-training execution. Marin publishes packed tasks in Parquet with explicit grader and environment identities. The current MarinSkyRL path expands selected tasks into many individual objects, builds equivalent Daytona snapshots again for each run, and discovers missing egress, resources, or judge configuration after rollout starts.

In the TaskTrove smoke, staging 1,273 tasks as 8,265 files held two H100 nodes idle for 58 minutes before Ray started. A capped 160-task export still required 2,685 objects and 18 minutes. The clean release contains 1,449,686 tasks but only 39 Docker environments, so data selection and environment reuse should be separate operations.

This issue owns the cross-repository contract. Dataset-specific validation remains in marin#9083. MarinSkyRL ingestion and sandbox lifecycle remain in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#540.

Done when:

- A post-training run selects packed tasks using a Parquet URI and metadata predicate, then unpacks only the assigned rows.
- An environment identity includes the Dockerfile, pinned verifier, and sandbox runtime interface. Equivalent environments reuse snapshots across runs and have an explicit cleanup policy.
- Tasks declare required capabilities such as network egress, judge access, and non-default resources. Launch fails before rollout when the selected runtime cannot provide them.
- Publish or launch validation can require an empty workspace to score zero and a shipped golden solution to score one.
- Trial results distinguish solution failure, grader failure, and infrastructure failure.
- Run provenance records the dataset release, selection predicate, verifier identity, and environment identity.
- One deterministic task and one judge task complete through the supported path without per-file corpus staging.

Verifier changes remain versioned with the dataset or environment identity. A wheel may reduce build cost. A training run must preserve the verifier pinned by the published task.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
The Grug MoE pipeline trainer added in #8739 always initializes fresh model parameters and Adam state. It cannot resume an interrupted run or emit a checkpoint for later training. Its JaxPP MPMD state is stage-local and contains model stages, optimizer state, and pending router-bias updates, so checkpoint I/O must preserve stage ownership without assembling the full model and optimizer state on each process. Expose an explicit checkpoint root and save cadence through the pipeline trainer configuration.

Done when:

- The `automatic_zero_bubble` and `automatic_dualpipe_v` schedules can save and restore model parameters, optimizer state, pending router-bias updates, and training step.
- Saving and restoring operate on stage-local shards and do not materialize the full training state on any process.
- A reduced round-trip test shows that one step after restore matches the corresponding uninterrupted step. Integer state must match exactly; loss and every floating model, optimizer, and router-bias leaf must have relative L2 error at most 0.002.
- An H100 smoke test resumes `automatic_zero_bubble` with PP2, EP8, and a replica axis of two across four H100x8 processes.
- The checkpoint layout and any topology restrictions are documented in `experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/README.md`.

Follow-up to #7024 and #8739. Run the H100 acceptance test with command buffers disabled; the command-buffer and DIME deadlock remains tracked in #7655.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Confirm the issue is actionable (clear "Done when" acceptance criteria)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PR; issue #8972 is the only tracking issue)
- [x] Root-cause the checkpoint gap in the #8739 pipeline trainer
- [x] Scope: **larger than a self-contained bug fix** → analysis for human review before implementation, no PR yet

## Research

The pipeline trainer never persists state. `_run_grug_local` initializes fresh params and Adam state every run ([`train.py:232-258`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/train.py#L232-L258)) and the loop keeps `step_index` as a Python local ([`train.py:321-345`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/train.py#L321-L345)) — nothing is written or read back.

The state that must round-trip is `GrugMoeAutomaticPipelineState`: per-stage `trainable_params`, `opt_state`, and `pending_qb_betas` ([`pipeline.py:209-217`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L209-L217)). Two structural facts constrain the design:

1. **It is genuinely stage-local.** Every leaf is a JaxPP `MpmdArray` pinned to one MPMD rank (`MpmdSharding(mesh_ids={stage_index})`, [`pipeline.py:374-390`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L374-L390)), and each process owns exactly one pipeline stage ([`pipeline.py:113-116`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L113-L116)). Save/restore can operate purely on each process's own shard — no gather needed, and the "do not materialize the full state on any process" criterion is both satisfiable and mandatory.
2. **Router bias is split out.** `split_automatic_stages` strips `router_bias` from `trainable_params`; the live values are folded from `pending_qb_betas` inside the step ([`pipeline.py:286-297`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L286-L297), [`pipeline.py:413-425`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L413-L425)). Persisting `pending_qb_betas` is therefore required for faithful resume — the static stages hold no bias to fall back on.

Two gaps beyond plumbing: there is **no training-step field** in the state (must be added to satisfy "restore … training step"), and `opt_state` carries rank-localized scalars that are empty on non-owning processes ([`pipeline.py:309-323`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L309-L323)) — save/restore must preserve that emptiness rather than densifying it.

## Proposed approach (for review before implementation)

**Save** — per process, per leaf: pull the process-local `jax.Array` from each `MpmdArray` via `to_mpmd_local_array` (the accessor the loss readout already uses, [`train.py:330-338`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/train.py#L330-L338)), guarded by `is_partially_addressable`, and write it under a stage-scoped path. Reuse Levanter's per-leaf tensorstore serializer ([`lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py`](lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py)) rather than a parallel writer; the local array carries a `NamedSharding` on `mpmd_mesh.unstack[stage_index]`, so it serializes without touching other ranks.

**Restore** — load each leaf into that same stage submesh sharding, then rewrap into an `MpmdArray` with the leaf's `MpmdSharding`, mirroring how init and `place_initial_scalar` build them ([`pipeline.py:337-350`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L337-L350), [`pipeline.py:592-610`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L592-L610)). Do **not** route restore through `spmd_to_mpmd_reshard` — that path materializes the full SPMD array first.

**Layout & topology** — one subdirectory per MPMD rank plus a small JSON manifest recording `stages`, `physical_stages`, `schedule`, `layer_counts`, `expert_axis_size`, and `replica_axis_size`. Restore asserts the manifest matches the current topology and fails fast otherwise; cross-topology resharding (different PP/EP) is out of scope and should be documented as a restriction. Integer leaves (Adam `count`, step) restore exactly; float leaves inherit the mp-policy param dtype, consistent with the ≤2e-3 relative-L2 acceptance bound.

**Config** — add explicit `checkpoint_root: str | None` and `save_steps: int` to `GrugPipelineTrainConfig` (no silent defaults), wire the `benchmark.py` env mapping, and load-or-init in `_run_grug_local`.

**Verification** — reduced round-trip test: run N steps, checkpoint, restore into a fresh process group, assert step N+1 matches the uninterrupted run (integers exact, floats ≤2e-3 rel-L2). The H100 acceptance (zero-bubble, PP2/EP8/replica2 across four H100x8, command buffers disabled per #7655) runs as a smoke test, not in CI.

**Estimated size:** new checkpoint module (~250-400 lines) + a step field in `GrugMoeAutomaticPipelineState` (touches the step signature and `dataclasses.replace` at [`pipeline.py:560-566`](experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/pipeline.py#L560-L566)) + config/loop wiring + round-trip test + README section. Multi-file and well over the 100-line bug-fix threshold, so I'm flagging for a human go-ahead before implementing.

Open questions for the owner: (a) checkpoint root — GCS path convention for these runs, or local-only for now? (b) is same-topology-only resume acceptable for v1, or is PP/EP resharding a hard requirement? (c) should `save_steps=0` mean "final only" or "never"?

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Track follow-up from #6572 for H100 BF16 fused linear softmax cross entropy at B=32768, H=2560, V=128256. The XLA reference materializes full logits/dlogits (`25.02 GiB` grad module) and measured `32.58ms` forward, `100.10ms` `jax.grad(loss_fn)`, `246,983 tok/s` combined.

The B-tiled custom VJP bounds memory while keeping full-vocab GEMMs. H100 autotune4 timings:

- B tile 2048: forward `34.19ms`, backward `135.08ms`, combined `193,585 tok/s`
- B tile 4096: forward `32.48-34.68ms`, backward `131.26-133.30ms`, combined `195k-200k tok/s`, grad memory `5.05 GiB`
- B tile 8192: forward `35.11ms`, backward `128.09ms`, combined `200,792 tok/s`
- B tile 16384: forward `33.06ms`, backward `122.90ms`, combined `210,107 tok/s`
- Production default 8192 on the clean PR branch: forward `33.73ms`, backward `123.56ms`, combined `208,323 tok/s`

### Definition of Done
- Explain the remaining backward gap against the materialized XLA reference and theoretical GEMM limits.
- Decide whether the production default should stay at 8192 or move with more memory evidence.
- Prototype the next kernel path if it can reduce passes over logits/dlogits without losing the memory win.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis (no PR — research/design task, depends on open PR #6572)**

The B-tile path lives in #6572, not on `main`. This is perf-investigation + a new kernel prototype, all gated on H100 hardware, so per the agent workflow this is an analysis for human review, not a code PR. Code refs below point at #6572's `pallas_gpu.py`.

# 1. Backward gap

The B-tiled backward is ~3 full-vocab GEMMs per tile; XLA `jax.grad` is ~2. The extra GEMM is a logits *recompute* — `_backward_b_tiled_from_lse` saves only LSE in residuals (the memory win), so it re-runs `x_block @ w` before computing dlogits, then does the two grad GEMMs (`dlogits @ wᵀ`, `xᵀ @ dlogits`).

Roofline at B=32768, H=2560, V=128256, bf16 — one GEMM = 2·B·H·V ≈ **21.5 TFLOP**:
- Forward (1 GEMM): observed ~33 ms → ~650 TFLOP/s ≈ 66% of H100 dense bf16 peak. GEMM-bound, near roofline; matches XLA forward (32.58 ms) as expected — same single GEMM either way.
- B-tiled backward (3 GEMMs = 64.5 TFLOP): ideal ~99 ms at fwd efficiency; observed 123 ms (default 8192) → ~525 TFLOP/s.
- XLA grad (2 GEMMs, logits already materialized): 100.10 ms, but pays 25.02 GiB HBM round-trips on logits/dlogits.

So the ~23 ms backward gap (123 vs 100 ms) ≈ the recompute GEMM. It is **not** inefficiency — it is the recompute-vs-materialize trade the memory bound buys. The path is already GEMM-bound; you can't close the gap without either storing logits (defeats the memory win) or removing the HBM round-trips of logits/dlogits via fusion (item 3).

**Relevant code (in #6572)**
- `_backward_b_tiled_from_lse` — recompute `x_block @ w`, then dlogits + 2 grad GEMMs per B-tile.
- `_linear_softmax_cross_entropy_loss_full_vocab_b_tiled` — forward, materializes one `[b_tile, V]` per tile.
- `_h100_full_vocab_b_tiled_block_size` — H100/bf16/B≥8192/V≥65536 policy gate, returns `_H100_FULL_VOCAB_B_TILED_BLOCK_SIZE = 8192`.

# 2. Production default: keep 8192

The reported B-tile sweep (193k → 210k tok/s from 2048 → 16384) is a tiling-overhead curve: bigger tiles → fewer `fori_loop` iters, larger GEMMs, better MXU utilization. But peak transient memory scales linearly with the tile — per-tile `[b_tile, V]` f32 logits + dlogits:
- 4096 ≈ 4.2 GiB (+ ~1.3 GiB f32 `grad_w` accumulator) → matches the reported 5.05 GiB.
- 8192 ≈ ~10 GiB; 16384 ≈ ~20 GiB.

16384 buys ~1% over 8192 (210k vs 208k tok/s) for ~2× peak logits memory, eroding most of the headroom under the 25 GiB XLA reference and squeezing co-resident activations. **Recommend the default stays 8192** unless a real memory budget shows ≥10 GiB free headroom at the target shape; revisit only with that evidence.

# 3. Next kernel path

The win is removing the logits/dlogits HBM round-trips, not removing a GEMM. The current B-tiled backward materializes full `[b_tile, V]` logits **and** dlogits to HBM (~8 GiB each at 16384). A fused Pallas kernel — B-tiled **and** V-streamed, FlashAttention-style — would keep each `[b_tile, v_block]` logit/dlogit tile in SRAM, fuse the recompute GEMM + softmax + dlogits + both grad accumulations, and never write the logit volume to HBM. That pushes backward from ~525 toward the ~650 TFLOP/s the forward already hits (~99 ms target), keeping the memory bound.

Template already in-tree: the forward `_linear_softmax_cross_entropy_loss_pallas_gpu_fa_style_streaming` and the V-streaming `_backward_streaming_from_lse` (used on the non-H100 path). The prototype is a backward analog that nests V-streaming inside the B-tile so both dims stay tiled in SRAM. Note the current forward/backward route through the materializing XLA reference because "JAX 0.10 Mosaic GPU does not lower the tiled pallas_call dot_general path" — so this path is blocked on Mosaic GPU lowering support and should be prototyped against that constraint.

Next steps for a human: (a) confirm the recompute-pass attribution with an H100 profile of the backward (expect ~1 GEMM-time of `x@w` recompute), (b) prototype the fused B-tiled+V-streamed backward once Mosaic GPU lowering lands, (c) re-sweep memory headroom before moving the 8192 default.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
`CloudGcpService` uses two GCP clients: a REST `httpx.Client` for the v2 TPU/compute/logging surfaces, and a gRPC `tpu_v2alpha1.TpuClient` used *only* for the four queued-resource (reserved-TPU) methods — `create/get/delete/list_queued_resources` (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/gcp/service.py`).

Consider porting those four methods onto the REST client so the class has a single transport, a single auth mechanism, and uniform error handling. That would also let us delete the lazy-init + lock around `_tpu_alpha_client` and drop the `google-cloud-tpu` dependency.

Trade-offs the implementer should weigh:
- Queued resources currently live on the `v2alpha1` surface, while the REST helpers target stable `v2`. Check whether queued resources are reachable on `v2` (GA) before committing — if so this is low-risk and reuses `_paginate` / `tpu_operation_status` directly; if not, a REST port means hand-built JSON on an alpha surface (field-churn risk) plus LRO wiring.
- The gRPC client currently provides typed request/response protos and pagination for free; REST would hand-assemble/parse those.
- The lazy gRPC client constructor resolves ADC eagerly, so any port must preserve the class's "construct cheaply, authenticate on first call" contract.

Not urgent — the lazy-init race was already fixed in #6435. This is a consistency/dependency cleanup; implementer decides scope and whether it's worth doing now.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Actionability check — actionable (named file/methods, clear definition of done)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR; #6435 already landed the lazy-init fix)
- [x] Resolve the central risk: are queued resources on GA `v2` REST?
- [x] Scope the port + post analysis
- [ ] Human decision on whether to implement now (scope left to implementer per issue)

# Research

The blocking question — *"Check whether queued resources are reachable on `v2` (GA) before committing"* — resolves **yes**. This is the low-risk branch the issue describes: the REST port reuses `_paginate` / `_classify_response` / `tpu_operation_status` directly, with no hand-built JSON on an alpha surface.

Evidence:
- Installed GA `google.cloud.tpu_v2` exposes the full queued-resource proto set: `CreateQueuedResourceRequest`, `GetQueuedResourceRequest`, `DeleteQueuedResourceRequest`, `ListQueuedResourcesRequest`, `QueuedResource`, `QueuedResourceState` (alpha only adds `PerformMaintenance…`).
- The `v2` REST reference page `projects.locations.queuedResources` exists (301-redirects, not 404).

**Relevant code**
- [`service.py#L669-L777`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/gcp/service.py#L669-L777) — the 4 gRPC methods + `_qr_api_error`
- [`service.py#L419-L425`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/gcp/service.py#L419-L425) — lazy `_tpu_alpha_client` to delete
- [`service.py#L535-L557`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/gcp/service.py#L535-L557) — `tpu_operation_status`, reusable for the create LRO
- [`pyproject.toml#L24`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/pyproject.toml#L24) — `google-cloud-tpu>=1.18.0` to drop
- [`test_gcp_service.py#L362-L395`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/tests/cluster/backends/gcp/test_gcp_service.py#L362-L395) — two MagicMock queued-resource tests

# Proposed approach

Port all four methods onto the REST `httpx.Client` at `{_TPU_BASE}/{parent}/queuedResources`, then delete the gRPC client, `_qr_api_error`, the `tpu_v2alpha1` / `google.api_core` imports, and the `google-cloud-tpu` dep.

- **create** — `POST …/queuedResources?queuedResourceId={name}` with body `{"tpu":{"nodeSpec":[{"parent":…,"nodeId":name,"node":{…}}]},"guaranteed":{"reserved":true}}`; classify via `_classify_response`. Matches current gRPC behavior, which fires the create and ignores the returned LRO. (Design note: if we later want fail-fast on queued-resource create like `tpu_create`, capture the op name and poll `tpu_operation_status` — out of scope unless wanted.)
- **describe** — `GET …/queuedResources/{name}`; `state = data["state"]["state"]` (default `"UNKNOWN"`); 404→None.
- **delete** — `DELETE …/queuedResources/{name}?force=true`; swallow 404.
- **list** — `_paginate(parent/queuedResources, "queuedResources")`; labels live at `tpu.nodeSpec[0].node.labels`; keep the wildcard-zone extraction from the resource name.
- **tests** — convert the two MagicMock tests to the existing `httpx.MockTransport` fake (consistent with the rest of the file); add create/describe/delete coverage asserting URL/params and 404→None.

Estimated ~120–180 lines incl. tests; net deletion of a transport, a dependency, and the lazy-client lock. `fake.py` (InMemory) is unaffected.

The issue says *"implementer decides scope and whether it's worth doing now."* The risk is now resolved and the change is mechanical, but it removes a dependency and migrates an API surface, so I'm flagging for a human go-ahead before opening a PR. Reply here to greenlight and I'll implement.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Rewrite implementation-pinned tests so they check public behavior instead of private representation, helper dispatch, or call counts.

Primary examples: lib/haliax/tests/test_named_ref.py, tests/execution/test_artifact_registry.py, tests/rl/test_replay_buffer.py, lib/levanter/tests/test_tokenizers.py, lib/haliax/tests/test_ragged_dot_dispatch.py, and lib/levanter/tests/kernels/test_pallas_fused_cross_entropy_loss.py.

### Definition of Done
- Private _prefix/_root/_is_rollout_fresh assertions are replaced by public behavior checks or a named public inspection API.
- Mock call-count assertions are secondary to observable files, results, warnings, or fake boundary state.
- Refactors that preserve behavior are less likely to break these tests.

Parent audit: #6424

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read the 6 implementation-pinned test files + the code they test
- [x] Scope decision: multi-module (haliax/levanter/marin), spans 6 files, includes a design question → **analysis-only, no PR** per the larger-than-bugfix rule
- [x] Post Research + per-file proposed rewrites for human review

# Research

Per parent audit #6424 finding #3 (S3) and #5 (S3/S8): these tests assert private representation (`_prefix`/`_ref`/`_root`), call directly into private helpers (`_is_rollout_fresh`), or assert mock call counts (`assert_not_called`/`assert_called_once`) as the *primary* signal. They break under behavior-preserving refactors and miss externally visible regressions.

Not opening a PR: this touches three modules and the cleanest fix for `NamedRef` raises a design question (is the composed-index encoding part of the contract, or test-only?) that the maintainer should decide first. Proposing per-file rewrites below; once an approach is picked I can split into per-module PRs.

**Relevant code**
- [`replay_buffer.py#L124`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/replay_buffer.py#L124) — `_is_rollout_fresh`; already observable via `add_batches`/`set_current_step`/`size`
- [`ref.py#L372-L379`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/ref.py#L372) — `slice()` builds `_prefix`; writes through it are the real contract
- [`test_tokenizers.py#L1474-L1542`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/tests/test_tokenizers.py#L1474) — staging dispatch asserted via mock call counts

# Proposed approach (per file)

**1. `tests/rl/test_replay_buffer.py:445` `test_is_rollout_fresh` — highest value, self-contained.**
Delete the private-method test. `create_test_batch` already accepts `weight_step=` and `timestamp=`, and the file at L403-442 already proves freshness through `add_batches` + `set_current_step(...)` + `size()`. Rewrite the four cases (step-window min, future weight_step, stale timestamp) as add-batches-then-assert-`size()`/`sample_rollouts()`. No private access; fails on real filtering regressions.

**2. `lib/levanter/tests/test_tokenizers.py:1474-1542` staging dispatch — replace call-count asserts with file provenance.**
Make each fake source write *distinguishable* bytes (mirror→`"MIRROR"`, hf→`"HF"`). Then assert the staged `tokenizer.json` *content* instead of `mock.assert_not_called()`:
- cache-hit: pre-seed cache, assert staged bytes are the cached ones (hf/mirror fakes that would write different bytes leave it unchanged);
- mirror-hit: staged bytes == mirror's;
- corrupt-mirror: mirror writes `"not json"`, assert final staged file is the valid hf copy.
Call counts may stay as a *secondary* assertion. Separately, the type-only tests at L356-420 (`isinstance(MarinTokenizer)`, `all_special_ids is list`, `encode_returns_list_of_ints`) are S2 tautologies already covered by the roundtrip tests at L438 — collapse them (keep the special-token-id constants; those are a real contract).

**3. `lib/haliax/tests/test_named_ref.py` — behavior vs public inspection API (design question).**
`test_dslice_combination_branches` (L85-148) and the `_prefix`/`_ref` asserts (L82, L169-170, L221) pin the internal slice encoding. The real contract is *index composition*: after `ds_ref.slice({...})`, writing a sentinel through the sub-ref should land in exactly the corresponding base-ref cells. Rewrite each branch as write-through-sub-ref → read base → assert affected/unaffected cells (covers dslice+slice, dslice+dslice, int, negative, list, array, strided composition without naming `dslice`). `unsliced._ref is base._ref` → assert a write through `unsliced` is visible in `base`. **Decision needed:** if the composed-index encoding is meant to be contract (e.g. for kernel authors), expose a public inspection API and assert that instead of `_prefix`.

**4. `lib/levanter/tests/kernels/test_pallas_fused_cross_entropy_loss.py:1107+` — low.**
`called["pallas"]==1`/`called["xla"]==1` already sit alongside a `pytest.warns(... "vmem compile OOM")` and the fallback path. Make the observable output primary (assert the returned loss equals the xla fake's result); keep counts secondary.

**5. `lib/haliax/tests/test_ragged_dot_dispatch.py` — low / partly no clean surface.**
`calls == [_DEFAULT_DIM_NUMS, _DLHS_DIM_NUMS, _DRHS_DIM_NUMS]` (L121) is redundant with the grad-correctness asserts above it (L118-120) — drop or soften it. `_triton_default_block_sizes` tests (L76-85) pin an internal heuristic with no public behavior; recommend leaving as explicit internal-heuristic guards or removing — there's no observable contract to convert them to.

**6. `tests/execution/test_artifact_registry.py` — low; file is mostly good already.**
`test_manifest_layout` (L137) reads `_root` but is really asserting the on-disk wire format, which *is* a cross-reader contract — keep (optionally via a small public path accessor). `test_root_normalizes_trailing_slash` (L156) and the `get_default_registry` `_root` checks (L261, L266) can instead assert via where a registered manifest lands (observable) rather than the private attr.

**Suggested batching:** (a) marin (`test_replay_buffer`, `test_artifact_registry`), (b) levanter (`test_tokenizers` staging, kernel fallback), (c) haliax (`test_named_ref`, `test_ragged_dot_dispatch`) — gated on the NamedRef decision. Items 1 and 2 are the highest leverage and lowest risk.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Replace runtime validation implemented with assert and narrow broad best-effort exception swallowing in Marin runtime paths.

Primary examples: lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/render.py, lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_worker.py, lib/marin/src/marin/rl/weight_transfer/arrow_flight.py, lib/marin/src/marin/transform/conversation/transform_conversation.py, lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/evalchemy_evaluator.py, and lib/marin/src/marin/execution/executor.py.

### Definition of Done
- Externally reachable validation raises explicit exceptions instead of assert.
- Intentional best-effort fallbacks catch expected exception types and log useful context.
- Tests cover the new validation/fallback behavior.

Parent audit: #6424

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — multi-module, no PR (per scope guidance).** This is a 6-file cleanup spanning four subsystems with a DoD requiring tests at each site, so it exceeds the self-contained single-PR bar. Recommend splitting into two focused PRs (below). Line numbers re-checked against current `main` (`81c92c6`) — three of the listed swallow sites are already narrowed and need no change.

# Research

Two distinct defects from audit #6424: `assert` used for externally-reachable validation (S7, vanishes under `python -O`), and broad `except Exception` with no logged context masking real failures (S6).

**S7 — assert as validation** ([render.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/environments/inference_ctx/render.py))
- L202 `Llama3Renderer._render_message` — `assert message.get("thinking") is None`; reachable from any caller passing a `thinking` message.
- L277 `Qwen3Renderer._render_message` — same assert.
- L326 `Qwen3Renderer._end_message_token` — `assert len(tokens) == 1`; tokenizer-config invariant, reachable via a tokenizer lacking a single `<|im_end|>` token.

**S6 — broad swallows still open**
- [rollout_worker.py#L624](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/rollout_worker.py#L624) — `except Exception: pass`, no log; transient run_state RPC failures are invisible.
- [arrow_flight.py#L93](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/weight_transfer/arrow_flight.py#L93) — `except Exception: pass` around the GCP metadata fetch; should narrow to `urllib.error.URLError`/`OSError`/`socket.timeout` and log at debug.
- [executor.py#L321](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/executor.py#L321) — `except Exception: return None` around `current_client()`; silently disables TPU region inference.

**Already narrowed on `main` — no action needed**
- [transform_conversation.py#L113](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/transform/conversation/transform_conversation.py#L113) — already `except json.JSONDecodeError` (keeps args raw). Only open question from the audit: tag-as-unparsed vs raw; raw is defensible, leave as-is unless product wants tagging.
- [evalchemy_evaluator.py#L96](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/evalchemy_evaluator.py#L96) (`_TeeWriter`) — already `except (OSError, ValueError)` with a teardown comment.
- [evalchemy_evaluator.py#L250](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/evalchemy_evaluator.py#L250) — outer already `logger.warning(...)`; only the nested `wandb.finish(exit_code=1)` swallow remains (acceptable teardown best-effort).

# Proposed Approach

**PR 1 (S7, testable, self-contained):** in `render.py` replace the three asserts with explicit exceptions carrying context — `NotImplementedError(f"CoT/thinking not supported in {type(self).__name__}")` for L202/L277, and `ValueError(f"Expected single token for <|im_end|>, got {len(tokens)}: {tokens}")` for L326. Tests: each renderer raises on a `thinking` message, and `_end_message_token` raises for a tokenizer that splits `<|im_end|>`.

**PR 2 (S6):** narrow + log the three open swallows. rollout_worker L624 → `except Exception: logger.debug("run_state check failed (best-effort)", exc_info=True)`; arrow_flight L93 → catch `(urllib.error.URLError, OSError, socket.timeout)` + debug log; executor L321 → debug log before `return None`. The fallback behavior is unchanged, so the only test worth adding is that the metadata-fetch helper falls back to hostname when the request raises; the rest is pure observability and warrants no test.

Holding here for a maintainer to confirm the split before implementing (esp. `NotImplementedError` vs `ValueError` for the CoT asserts, and whether transform_conversation should tag unparsed args).
